Subject: Follow-up: POC call — SLO comparators we discussed

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the call earlier — the Helix execs appreciated the demo. A few follow-ups from our side so we can finalize the POC success criteria: 

- We need a short table comparing how Redwood handles availability and throttling vs the major hyperscalers (AWS/GCP/Azure): typical uptime SLAs observed in your hosted tier, how rate limits are enforced per-tenant, and what the expected error budget looks like for a 30-day window.
- Clarify failover behavior: if a single region loses GPU capacity, what happens to in-flight requests? How does KV/prefix cache affect cold-starts during failover? 
- For our compliance team: outline where audit logs live in Redwood Private (retention defaults and ability to ship to our SIEM).

Can you share a short one-pager and a proposed test matrix we can run during the POC (we want to validate uptime under two load profiles and simulate regional outage)?

Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC call — SLO comparators we discussed

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Recap + attachments below.

Recap of asks:
- Comparative table: uptime/observed SLO deltas vs hyperscalers, error budget calc for 30-day window, rate limit behavior.
- Failover/cold-start behavior and KV cache implications.
- Audit log retention and delivery options for Private.
- Proposed test matrix for two load profiles + regional outage sim.

What I attached:
- Redwood-SLO-onepager.pdf (one-page summary of our production SLOs, fallback tiers, and error-budget math)
- helix-poc-test-matrix.xlsx (proposed test cases, metrics to capture, owners)
- redwood-fallback-diagram.png (high-level flow for fallthrough routing between model variants/regions)

Quick answers inline:
- Uptime: hosted customers typically see 99.95% regional availability baseline; Dedicated customers are commonly contracted to 99.99% with reserved capacity. Hyperscaler managed endpoints often advertise similar SLAs but vary in observed degradations when their control plane is overloaded — our differentiated behavior is graceful fallthrough to compatible model variants and cross-region routing that preserves KV cache for pinned sessions when possible.
- Rate limits: we enforce per-API-key concurrency and per-minute token throughput. For Dedicated/Private we offer configurable quotas and token bursting policies. We can expose a temporary elevated quota for the POC run.
- Failover: in-flight requests are retried on compatible hosts with idempotency hints; KV cache warming is handled with a best-effort async prefetch for pinned sessions. Cold-start latency is higher on first retries but decays quickly with prefix caching.

Next steps I propose:
1) Align on two load profiles and dates for the POC tests (I put tentative dates/actions in the spreadsheet).
2) Technical sync with our reliability lead (Ben) to finalize probes and synthetic traffic.
3) Procurement thread to confirm contract guardrails for fallthrough behavior and audit delivery.

I'll be available Friday for a short technical sync.

- Marcus
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redwood-SLO-onepager.pdf (pdf)]

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC call — SLO comparators we discussed

Aisha / Marcus — added a few technical clarifications for the test matrix:

- Rate limiting details: for our hosted API we default to a soft concurrency limit per API key and a token-per-minute cap. During the POC we can run with a dedicated token that maps to a dedicated pod pool to avoid noisy neighbor effects; this will let you see near-dedicated performance without full Dedicated capacity.
- Error budget calc we recommend: use total successful request tokens / total attempted tokens over 30 days and apply 99.95% availability baseline for hosted. I'll include sample scripts for measuring 5xx rates and tail latency in the drive folder.
- Failover plan: to simulate regional loss we recommend a two-step approach in the tests: 1) drain capacity in the region (synthetic outage) and 2) validate routing to fallback region while monitoring request success and KV-hit rates. Expect an initial latency spike (200–600ms extra) for sessions that require KV reconstruction.

I attached a small check-list in the sheet. Marcus — can we have a short runbook entry for the Helix POC that spells out the steps and who flips which switches?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: HelixHealth POC — contract & liability questions

Hi — quick response to help legal and procurement move forward, and proposed next steps.

Answers in brief:
- Compensable breach: we define an SLA breach for Hosted as sustained unavailability beyond the committed uptime (e.g., below 99.95% over the billing window) caused by Redwood-managed infrastructure; credits are calculated pro-rata on affected usage. For Dedicated the target and credit formula are stated in the reserved capacity agreement. We'll provide the exact clause language for the draft.
- Fallthrough behavior: degraded routing to fallback model variants is considered graceful degradation. If the degradation results in sustained unavailability (requests failing or not returning within the response SLO), that would be treated under the SLA. Short-lived fallthroughs (e.g., routing to a lower-capacity variant with higher latency but successful responses) are not typically treated as SLA violations unless they cause the availability calculation to fall below the committed target.
- Audit logs: for Private we support raw audit log export to S3 (or your object store) with configurable retention; default retention is 90 days, extended retention can be negotiated. Logs include request/response meta, auth events, and routing/fallback metadata.

Next steps:
1) I'll share formal clause language and a short SLA appendix by EOD Monday.
2) Ben — can you draft the short POC runbook that lists who triggers the regional drain and who validates KV-hit metrics?
3) Schedule a 30-minute legal + tech alignment next Tuesday; I included a Doodle link in the drive folder.

Thanks — we'll keep this tight so Helix can start the tests next week.

- Marcus
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
